profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a plaintiff-side employment law firm preparing a partner briefing package for a potential class and representative action against a food-delivery platform that manages couriers through ratings, batching, acceptance metrics, and automated deactivation. The team is using recent scholarship on algorithmic management in app-work to sharpen factual themes, but the immediate work product is a practical internal package for a go/no-go decision and an upcoming co-counsel call. The agenda is to align on interfaces between legal research and fact development: what Marcus will deliver on algorithmic-control authorities, which worker statement set both will mine for quotations, how the shared chronology will be populated, and what 'ready for partner review' means by Thursday. The expected outcome is an apparently clear handoff plan for a research component, declaration summaries, and a chronology/exhibit structure that both believe will integrate smoothly into one partner-facing package.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Wage-and-hour class actions, worker classification, pre-certification case strategy, drafting partner-facing legal memoranda
members.background: Elena has six years at a labor and employment boutique and previously clerked for a state appellate judge; she is known for converting sprawling factual and policy material into concise litigation narratives that partners can use quickly.
members.private_state: Elena wants to give the partner a compact, litigation-ready package that supports a fast strategic decision without inviting a broader theory debate, and she is concerned that diffuse background material will make the matter look underdeveloped.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says the package should synthesize the key authorities on algorithmic control, 'authorities' means binding or at least citable legal sources such as cases, statutes, regulations, and agency materials rather than academic literature.

The latest declarations packet is the Friday evening intake compilation in the litigation workspace with declarants labeled D1-D6, and anything in side folders or weekend notes is supplemental unless expressly adopted into that packet.

A draft is ready for partner review only when it can be read as a near-final work product, with citations checked, adverse authority flagged, and no obvious placeholders or unresolved structural issues.

The shared chronology is a pleading-oriented fact chron limited to worker events, platform communications, and policy changes that could plausibly support declarations, a complaint, or class allegations.

members.name: Marcus Iqbal
members.expertise: Employment law research, comparative regulatory tracking, evidence organization, cross-matter knowledge systems
members.background: Marcus spent a decade as a research attorney before moving into knowledge management for a national plaintiffs' firm, where he builds reusable issue maps and source banks for novel employment theories and emerging workplace technologies.
members.private_state: Marcus wants to preserve nuance from the app-work literature so the firm does not collapse distinct platform models too early, and he is concerned that a too-narrow legal summary will underprepare the team for pleading, expert, and policy-facing arguments later.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says they need the key authorities on algorithmic control, 'authorities' naturally includes the academic taxonomy distinguishing app-work from crowdwork and capital platform work, because that framework shapes how legal facts are interpreted even if it is not binding law.

The latest declarations packet is the reorganized worker binder in the knowledge folder that incorporates weekend interview notes and cleaned excerpts, because once materials are normalized for issue-tracking they become the operative packet for downstream synthesis.
A draft is ready for partner review once the analytical structure is substantively complete and the linked source trail is in place, even if some pin cites, formatting, or attachment cleanup remain.

The shared chronology is an issue chron that should absorb not only worker events but also app-interface changes, regulator actions, and external materials that explain the evolution of algorithmic control.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the 'key authorities' on algorithmic control
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Marcus will synthesize the key authorities on algorithmic control for Elena to incorporate into the partner package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena hears 'key authorities' as the controlling and persuasive legal materials she can safely cite in a partner-facing strategy note: case law on control and classification, wage-order provisions, agency guidance, and perhaps regulator settlements.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus hears 'key authorities' as the full set of serious interpretive sources that matter for framing the issue, including the academic literature on app-work and algorithmic management, especially the taxonomy separating app-work from crowdwork and capital platform work.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'key authorities' sounds unusually precise in a legal setting, so both assume they are invoking the same professional shorthand; because no one asks for a source list in the meeting, the disagreement stays hidden behind a shared commitment to synthesis.

misalignment_points.topic: Which worker statement set is the 'latest declarations packet'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to pulling the top three quotes from the latest declarations packet.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the Friday intake packet in the litigation workspace, containing the six worker declarations in their numbered litigation order and excluding the weekend interviewer annotations unless separately elevated.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the Sunday reorganized binder in the knowledge folder, where the same workers are arranged by issue theme and supplemented with weekend interview notes and clipped excerpts for quick retrieval.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The packets overlap heavily in substance, and during the meeting they only discuss pulling 'the top three quotes' rather than citing page numbers, file names, or folder paths, so the reference feels safely shared even though each is picturing a different packet.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as 'ready for partner review'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the memo component and chronology should be ready for partner review by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena believes 'ready for partner review' means near-final: cleaned citations, adverse points flagged, integrated references to the declaration summaries, and prose that can be read straight through without explanation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus believes 'ready for partner review' means the analysis is mature enough for strategic discussion, with placeholders and some citation cleanup acceptable if the architecture and source links are already there.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In law-firm practice, partner review can refer either to a polished near-final draft or to an informed strategy draft, and because the conversation focuses on Thursday as a coordination milestone rather than on quality thresholds, each silently imports their own standard.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Elena will own the chronology and Marcus will add the algorithmic-management materials.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes the chronology is a fact chron for the case file, limited to dated worker experiences, onboarding steps, pay or dispatch changes, deactivations, and platform communications that could matter in pleadings or declarations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus assumes the chronology is an issue chron, so his additions should include app-screen revisions, regulator developments, and even dated external framing materials that help explain how the platform's control mechanisms changed over time.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both kinds of chronology are common in litigation teams and often share the same spreadsheet shell, so dividing responsibility by contribution rather than by content boundaries creates a natural illusion of agreement.
